findings.evidence: PairEval.lean:293-306 vs 343-362 vs 368-387: the three proofs differ only in the family, the series-level lemma rewritten in, and the resulting value.
findings.fix: Add one private lemma, e.g. `private theorem eval₂_subst_formalAdd {fam : Unit ⊕ Unit → MvPowerSeries Unit O} (hfam : HasSubst fam) {t u₁ u₂ : O} (ht : PowerSeries.HasEval t) (h₁ : PowerSeries.HasEval u₁) (h₂ : PowerSeries.HasEval u₂) (hval : (fun s ↦ MvPowerSeries.eval₂ (RingHom.id O) (fun _ : Unit ↦ t) (fam s)) = Sum.elim (fun _ ↦ u₁) fun _ ↦ u₂) : MvPowerSeries.eval₂ (RingHom.id O) (fun _ : Unit ↦ t) (subst fam W.formalAdd) = W.formalAddEval u₁ u₂`, and reduce all three theorems to supplying `hval` plus the series-level identity.
findings.issue: formalAddEval_zero_right (341-362), formalAddEval_zero_left (366-387) and the existing formalAddEval_formalInverseEval (288-306) are three copies of one skeleton: hfam, then `simp only [coe_aeval, algebraMap_self, hfam]; exact hasEval_pair …`, then `aeval_subst … (continuous_aeval (PowerSeries.hasEval ht)) hev W.formalAdd`, then `rw` the series-level law, then `simpa [formalAddEval, coe_aeval, …, hfam] using h.symm`. The reusable fact — evaluating a substituted formalAdd at t is formalAddEval at the evaluated pair — stays hidden inside each proof.

findings.evidence: Substitution.lean:164-166 states `hasSubst_pair` for `Sum.elim (fun _ ↦ q₁) (fun _ ↦ q₂)`; Add/Unit.lean:252-254 states `subst_unitR_formalAdd` for `Sum.elim X (fun _ ↦ 0)`; Add/Inverse.lean:94-101 exists solely to convert between the two spellings, and Add/Assoc.lean:197-199 comments on the same point.
findings.fix: Ascribe the intended spelling at the witness, e.g. `(hasSubst_pair (by simp) (by simp) : HasSubst (Sum.elim X (fun _ ↦ 0) : Unit ⊕ Unit → MvPowerSeries Unit O))`, or bridge with an explicit `funext` reshape, and note why — matching `invPair_eq`.
findings.issue: `hasSubst_pair (q₁ := X ()) (q₂ := 0)` has family `Sum.elim (fun _ ↦ X ()) (fun _ ↦ 0)`, but `hev`, the `rw [W.subst_unitR_formalAdd]` at line 360 and the `hfam` rewrite all speak of `Sum.elim X (fun _ ↦ 0)`. The step works only through Unit-eta defeq between `X` and `fun _ ↦ X ()`, with no comment. Same at lines 383/385 for the left law.

findings.evidence: `PowerSeries.X_apply : X (R := R) = MvPowerSeries.X () := rfl` at mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Basic.lean:161, used by this development at Add/Unit.lean:302.
findings.fix: Replace `PowerSeries.X` by `PowerSeries.X_apply` in both simp sets (`MvPowerSeries.eval₂_X` is already `@[simp]` and can go).
findings.issue: The closing `simpa` passes the definition `PowerSeries.X` to unfold it into `MvPowerSeries.X ()` so that `eval₂_X` applies; likewise at line 386. Unfolding a definition in a simp set is less stable than the named lemma for the same equation.

summary: The two new proofs replicate, twice over, the same 20-line transport skeleton already present in formalAddEval_formalInverseEval instead of factoring it into a private lemma, and both bridge the hasSubst_pair family spelling to Add/Unit.lean's spelling by undocumented definitional equality — the exact mismatch that Add/Inverse.lean and Add/Assoc.lean handle with an explicit, commented reshape.
